record.summary: Requires developers of generative AI systems or services made available to Californians to post on their websites documentation of the data used to train them, including a high-level summary of the datasets used: for example, whether they include data protected by copyright, trademark or patent, or are entirely in the public domain. Developers had to post the documentation on or before 1 Jan 2026 for systems released on or after 1 Jan 2022.
record.notes: Signed on 28 Sep 2024 as Chapter 817, Statutes of 2024; the Governor's release of 29 Sep 2024 lists it among the 17 bills on generative AI that he had signed over the previous 30 days. The duty is codified in Civil Code section 3111. Compliance required from 1 Jan 2026.

verification.note: Recheck of 18 Oct 2026. Stored and read: the Governor's legislative update of 28 Sep 2024 (gov.ca.gov), which lists 'AB 2013 ... Generative artificial intelligence: training data transparency' among the bills he signed that day; his release of 29 Sep 2024 (gov.ca.gov, copy of 17 Oct 2026), which lists it among the bills on generative AI signed over the previous 30 days; and the Senate Judiciary Committee's analysis of AB 412 (hearing of 23 Jun 2026, sjud.senate.ca.gov), which gives the chapter (Ch. 817, Stats. 2024) and describes Civil Code section 3111 as existing law, with the deadline of 1 Jan 2026 and systems released on or after 1 Jan 2022. That analysis once calls the law the 'California AI Transparency Act', the name of SB 942 (US-CA-02); the record keeps the bill's subject title. The statute's text on leginfo.legislature.ca.gov refused automated downloads (HTTP 403), so the summary rests on the committee's description of section 3111 rather than on the statute itself, and the version 1 list of required contents (sources, data types, personal data, processing) was narrowed to what the analysis states. Version 1's notes on a federal lawsuit by xAI and on the House Great American AI Act discussion draft rested on secondary sources only and were removed.

judgment.status_reasoning: Signed on 28 Sep 2024 (legislative update of that day). The Senate Judiciary Committee analysis heard on 23 Jun 2026 describes the duty as existing law: developers must post the summary 'on or before January 1, 2026'. That date has passed (today 18 Oct 2026), so 'In force' stands. No stored file shows a repeal, a delay or a court order against the law; the reported xAI lawsuit stays an open question.
judgment.date_reasoning: date_published 2024-09-28: the update dated Sep 28, 2024 says the Governor 'today announced that he has signed the following bills' and lists AB 2013. date_in_force 2026-01-01 is the statutory deadline for posting the documentation, as the analysis states it.
judgment.scope_reasoning: An AI-specific state law on transparency of generative AI training data; in scope with no note.

open_questions: Version 1 noted a federal lawsuit by xAI against AB 2013 (C.D. Cal., end of 2025) from a secondary source; no stored file confirms it or says whether enforcement was enjoined. A later run could store the court docket or an official notice to check whether the status needs a note.

The summary rests on the Senate Judiciary Committee's description of Civil Code section 3111, not on the statute: leginfo.legislature.ca.gov refuses automated downloads. A person could provide the chaptered text (AGENTS.md section 7.8) so that the full list of required contents can be quoted.
